economic_definition: Telephone sets of all kinds - the complete 8517.1x group. Economically one product class throughout: a telephone handset. The HS2022 split only separates smartphones from feature phones WITHIN that class. AMENDED 29-Aug-2026 under approved Change Proposal 001: 851711 and 851718 are included because the Jan-2022 customs-tariff transition pushed cellular handsets into those residual lines. Non-cellular content is immaterial in undisturbed months - Dec-2021 851711+851718 = 1.71 against 851712 = 775.78, i.e. 0.22 percent of the basket.
continuity_rationale: TWO transitions were observed, not one. (1) JANUARY 2022 - Customs Tariff moved to HS2022 on 01.01.2022 while the DGCI&S statistical directory still offered only HS2017 codes, so HS2022 declarations were mapped onto the nearest legacy codes: 851712 halved (775.78 to 230.90) while 851718 rose 196-fold (1.39 to 272.16) and 851711 rose 103-fold (0.32 to 33.06), with NO new codes appearing. A 196-fold jump in 'other telephone sets' is a classification artefact, not an economic event. (2) APRIL 2022 - DGCI&S directory switch: 851713 and 851714 first appear, 851770 falls to exactly 0.00 and is replaced by 851771/851779, and heading 8524 appears. Jan-Mar 2022 is therefore a contamination window in which the flow is split across 851711, 851712 and 851718. The five-code union is closed under BOTH transitions. The originally locked three-code union showed a 70 percent collapse into Jan-2022 and understated Mar-2022 by 38 percent - pure artefact, and it sat inside B1's post-intervention window where it would have biased beta3 directly.
break_points_checked: Jan-2022: VERIFIED transition (tariff). Apr-2022: VERIFIED transition (statistical directory). Apr-2024: VERIFIED no HS-6 change - the documented 85176240/85176950 deletions are 8-digit only. Apr-2026: VERIFIED no change. Undated intermediate 8-digit change 2017-2021: FLAGGED - immaterial at HS-6.
